title: In Vitro Skin Fibrosis Model for Antifibrotic Compound Screening
author: Alsharabasy, Pandit
materials: The preparation needs to be performed in Class II biological hood with standard aseptic technique.

steps.title: General laboratory preparations
steps.instruction: Prepare the workspace and reagents before starting the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Keep all stock solutions for hydrogel preparation at 4 °C; do not warm them before the primary procedures.
Refer to the key resources table for the complete list of materials.
Perform all procedures in a Class II biological hood using standard aseptic technique.
Culture cells (with or without seeding to hydrogels) at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare media, buffers, and growth factor
steps.instruction: Make all required media, buffers, and growth‑factor solutions.

substeps.instruction: Perform the preparation inside a Class II biological hood using standard aseptic technique.

steps.title: Extract proteins from hydrogel
steps.instruction: Wash, degrade, and lyse cells from collagen hydrogels for SDS‑PAGE and western blot analysis (total time 4–5 h).

substeps.instruction: Discard the culture medium from the top of each hydrogel well.
Add approximately 150 µL DPBS to each well, incubate 30 s, then discard the DPBS. Repeat this wash once, taking care not to discard the transparent hydrogel.
Add 100 µL collagenase to each hydrogel and incubate at 37 °C for 45 min.
Add 100 µL FBS‑containing medium and mix well by pipetting to inhibit collagenase activity.
Aspirate the entire solution into tapered 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
If cells remain attached to the well bottom, add 30 µL trypsin, incubate 5 min, neutralize with 60 µL medium, aspirate, and combine with the solution from the previous step.
Centrifuge the tubes at 200 × g, 4 °C for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Place the cell pellets on ice for 10 min before lysis.
Wash each pellet twice with 500 µL cold PBS, discarding the wash each time.
Add 30 µL lysis buffer to each pellet, vortex 10 s, and incubate on ice for 20 min.
Transfer the supernatants to pre‑cooled Eppendorf tubes and store at –80 °C until analysis.

description: The generation of an in vitro 3D fibrosis model consists of three main stages: (1) primary induction of fibrosis in flask; (2) fabrication of collagen hydrogels; and (3) loading of the hydrogel with cells and fibrosis induction (Figure 1).
